comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Parked rather than dropped, and the reason it is not urgent is on a new
card: `done` is idle on a pane nobody saw, and Muster holds both halves
of that - the core sees every working -> idle transition, and the shell
knows whether its own window had focus. See a_27TdrJVUb. This card is
the upstream ask, worth making only if we ever approach the herdr team.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
herdr computes 'done' as idle-on-an-unseen-pane, and seen-ness depends on the foreground client's outer_terminal_focus. A client feeds that only by sending DEC focus sequences (CSI I / CSI O) in its raw input stream, or the equivalent client-protocol message - the JSON API has no method, and sending those bytes through terminal.input reaches the pane's program instead (verified: docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 3).

Consequence: an agent that finishes while a Muster window sits unfocused gets marked seen by nobody, so it reads idle instead of done. Attention routing is the reason this project exists, so a false idle is not cosmetic.

Muster can drive the daemon's active tab via pane.focus, which covers the common case. The gap is window-level focus. Options: speak herdr's client protocol alongside the JSON API, or ask upstream for a method - herdr's own guardrail says shared runtime facts belong in server state behind the JSON API, so the ask rides their stated direction.
title: Upstream: no API for reporting client window focus
